newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana cocoa sales up in '96, gold stays top earner.
newsitem.headline: Ghana cocoa sales up in '96, gold stays top earner.

text.p: Gold remained Ghana's top foreign exchange earner in 1996 despite a bumper cocoa crop, government and central bank data showed on Wednesday.

Gold exports totalled $582.9 million in 1996 against $568.2 million for cocoa beans and products, according to the 1996 annual report published in the ministry of trade and industry's Ghana Export Bulletin.
The latest figures showed the gap between gold and cocoa earnings closed sharply from 1995.
The Ghana Export Bulletin only began collating data in July 1995, but complete 1995 data from the Bank of Ghana Annual Report showed cocoa exports amounted to $389.5 million against $647.3 for gold.
Ministry of Finance figures last month gave different gold and cocoa earnings figures.
Provisional 1996 balance of payments data presented to parliament in February for the 1997 budget showed gold earnings of $612.4 million against $508.6 million for cocoa.

Comparable year-on gold export volumes were not immediately available. Ghana Export Bulletin data showed the volume of gold exports in 1996 totalled 51,923 kg while Bank of Ghana data showed 1,689,470 fine ounces were exported.
Cocoa exports totalled 338,500 tonnes of cocoa beans in 1996 against 237,300 tonnes in 1995, while 51,400 tonnes of cocoa products where exported against 13,900 tonnes, the same sources showed.
Ghana has predicted a lower 1996/97 (October-September) cocoa harvest than in 1995/96. Forecasts for 1997/98 depend on weather and tree development later this year.
Ghana's 1998 gold production is set to rise with the opening of at least two new major mines before the end of the year.
